documents.title: METFORMIN HYDROCHLORIDE TABLET, FILM COATED — Lactic Acidosis
documents.text:
DailyMed — METFORMIN HYDROCHLORIDE TABLET, FILM COATED (NDA 020357)

WARNINGS AND PRECAUTIONS
5.1 Lactic Acidosis
There have been postmarketing reports of metformin-associated lactic acidosis in patients
with severe renal impairment (eGFR below 30 mL/min/1.73 m2), including fatal cases.
Metformin accumulation during renal impairment increases the risk of lactic acidosis.
Assessment of renal function is recommended before initiation and at least annually thereafter.

5.2 Contraindications
Metformin hydrochloride tablets are contraindicated in patients with an eGFR below 30 mL/min/1.73 m2.

documents.title: Risk of lactic acidosis with metformin in reduced kidney function
documents.text:
PubMed — PMCID: PMC7784512 — "Risk of lactic acidosis with metformin in reduced kidney function:
a retrospective cohort study" (Journal of Clinical Pharmacology, 2024).

Abstract
BACKGROUND: Metformin is widely prescribed, but its use in patients with reduced kidney function remains debated.
METHODS: We followed 41,208 adults with renal impairment (eGFR 30-59 mL/min/1.73 m2) who received metformin
or a sulfonylurea for a median of 3.2 years.
RESULTS: Metformin use was associated with an increased incidence of lactic acidosis compared with sulfonylurea
(adjusted hazard ratio 1.42, 95% CI 1.18-1.71). The absolute risk remained low (2.1 vs 1.5 events per 1000 person-years).
CONCLUSIONS: In adults with renal impairment, metformin exposure was associated with a higher rate of lactic acidosis.
